newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-FALDO CALLS ON OLD PUTTER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO CALLS ON OLD PUTTER.

text.p: Nick Faldo has turned to an old putter that he used to win three majors with at the turn of the decade to boost his bid for a fourth British Open title at Royal Troon this week.
The big Briton, who will turn 40 on Friday, has gone back to his workshop and hauled out the putter that helped him to the 1989 and 1990 U.S. Masters titles and the 1990 Open title at Muirfield.
"There's still some magic in it. I've been stroking the putts a lot better with it," he said. "It's been loitering in the workshop, now it's back in the bag."
Faldo added: " I'm striking the ball a lot better and I'm starting to hole some medium to long putts as well."
Faldo, whose sole victory this year came in the Nissan Open in Los Angeles early in March, feels his game has been "just a little bit under".
"In some areas I feel about 10 per cent off. That makes a big difference in this game, a major difference.
"Normally, I can get by with the occasional mistake and scramble my way out of it. Lately, I've been making a few more mistakes and not scrambling so well.
"I just need to find consistency. When I play well, it is as good as anything but my consistency hasn't been as good."
He denied a suggestion in a British newspaper at the weekend that his desire was waning.
"I wouldn't be out here if it wasn't high. I still work hard, practise hard and train hard and I love it," said Faldo, who has a reputation for meticulous preparation.
"Every time I hit a shot, I'm trying to hit it how I want to hit it. If I don't, as long as I go back to the practice ground to sort it out, I'll keep going.
"The day I don't want to sort it out, that will be it."
Faldo, who will be playing in his 22nd consecutive Open, said he could not remember one when so many of the top players were playing so well coming into the event.
"I think Ernie (Els), Tom Lehman and Nick Price plus of course Tiger (Woods) are all playing well right now. So if these guys carry on, they are the guys who should be right up there."
He did not discount compatriot Colin Montgomerie, who is playing at the course in the town where he lived as a child and who finished second at the U.S. Open last month.
"He is getting closer and closer," Faldo said. "He might have a good advantage with his local knowledge of the greens. That could help him tremendously this week."
Faldo said he expected there would be some rough weather this week after three practice days mixed with wind and rain.
"You will have to be a strong ball striker to survive four days of it," he said.
With his three titles, Faldo was asked his opinion of the five won by Tom Watson, including the 1982 Open on the same Royal Troon course.

"He did it in such a short time span (nine years) as well," Faldo said. "He was totally dominant because he was such a strong ball striker in the wind. He hit it very solidly and he was the best putter by miles."
